question.text: A portfolio manager takes a LONG position in stocks in a rising trend and SHORT positions in stocks in a declining trend, relying mainly on price-volume data. Which strategy is this?

explanation.text: The Logic: Momentum investing bets on continuation of ongoing trends, captured via price-volume signals — long winners, short losers. The Trap: Growth investing looks at fundamental earnings-growth; value at mispricing vs intrinsic value. Both are fundamental, not price-action based. Cross-Exam Context: XV Ch 15 (Technical Analysis) treats momentum in greater depth; XXI-B uses it at portfolio-strategy level. Manager's Pro-Tip: Momentum crashes violently at trend reversals — discipline around stop-losses is more important than entry rules.
